impact: bsdutils ships only logger, renice, script/scriptreplay and setpriv, none of which the worker shells out to; the util-linux CVEs are attributed here because the binary package shares the util-linux source. CVE-2026-76642 needs a privileged external mount helper, CVE-2026-78408 needs nsenter with cgroup write access, and CVE-2026-78409/78410 need a privileged X-mount.* helper or a restricted bind mount, so every trigger sits behind CAP_SYS_ADMIN and a mount operation this image never performs (uid 65534, cap-drop ALL, no privileged mode). This waiver is removed once the upstream Debian package carries the fix.

CVE-2026-92542 is Swarm VXLAN/IPsec data-path code inside the vendored moby tree; the CLI never creates or joins a swarm and the worker only runs docker run/exec/logs/inspect/pull/image inspect against the host socket. CVE-2026-92543 is the insecure-registry classifier: the worker passes no --insecure-registry (daemon configuration belongs to the host operator) and pulls only the digest-pinned silkeh toolchain image, so a forged DNS answer set cannot substitute image content. This waiver is removed once the upstream Debian package carries the fix.

git is a real worker dependency, but only through fixed `git init --bare`, `fetch <local bundle>`, `rev-parse`, `cat-file`, `ls-tree` and `diff` templates against a read-only bare repository materialised from an operator-provided case bundle. CVE-2026-105437 (merge size overflow), CVE-2026-111760 (recursive submodule clone) and CVE-2026-114466 (fast-import) require merge, submodule and fast-import entry points the worker never invokes, and no remote transport or network fetch is involved. This waiver is removed once the upstream Debian package carries the fix.

This waiver is removed once the upstream Debian package carries the fix.

libacl is pulled in by coreutils for ACL-preserving file operations. CVE-2026-54369 requires a privileged caller to resolve an attacker-controlled path whose components may be symlinks; the worker runs as 65534 with no setuid helper and only touches run/staging directories it just created, so there is no privilege boundary to escalate across. This waiver is removed once the upstream Debian package carries the fix.

libblkid only probes block devices and is reached through libmount or lsblk; the worker never enumerates or probes block devices, and /dev is the Docker default. The util-linux CVEs need a privileged mount path (external helper post-hook, nsenter --join-cgroup, X-mount.subdir resolution, restricted bind mounting), all of which require CAP_SYS_ADMIN that this container drops. This waiver is removed once the upstream Debian package carries the fix.

libcurl is linked by git for TLS; this image never runs the curl CLI, so CVE-2026-12064 (schemeless URL plus --proto-default sftp/scp) has no entry point. CVE-2026-8458 needs Negotiate-authenticated connection reuse, but no Negotiate or GSSAPI credentials exist in the container and git only reads local bundle files, so the connection pool sees no authenticated reconnects. This waiver is removed once the upstream Debian package carries the fix.

expat is present only as a dependency of Python's pyexpat extension. The control plane parses JSON contracts and case materials; no code path in src/ feeds attacker-supplied XML to expat (ElementTree is used by ci_gates only on locally produced JUnit files). All four CVEs are denial of service in XML_ParserReset memory tracking, entity amplification, external-entity dereference and attribute parsing, each requiring an XML document the worker never accepts. This waiver is removed once the upstream Debian package carries the fix.

libgssapi-krb5-2 is the GSSAPI shim reached only through libcurl's Negotiate support. The container has no KDC, no keytab and no krb5.conf naming a realm, and every git call uses a local bundle path, so no GSSAPI context is ever established. The fourteen krb5 CVEs are KDC/kadmind request-handling DoS or CAMMAC/authorization-indicator manipulation that only trigger in a client of an attacker-influenced realm. This waiver is removed once the upstream Debian package carries the fix.

libk5crypto3 provides the AES/DES/RC4 primitives behind libkrb5 for the krb5 stack. Nothing in this image initialises a krb5 context: there is no keytab, no ccache and no KDC configuration, and the worker never performs a Kerberos exchange. The fourteen CVEs are reached through KDC/kadmind ASN.1 and RPC decoding on the server side, which no process in this image implements. This waiver is removed once the upstream Debian package carries the fix.

libkrb5-3 holds the core Kerberos protocol implementation (ASN.1, preauth, PAC and keytab handling). It is linked but never initialised here: the container carries no keytab, no credential cache and no realm, and git never contacts a KDC because case repositories are read from local bundles. The fourteen CVEs are unauthenticated KDC/kadmind DoS and auth-indicator tampering that require the peer to be a KDC. This waiver is removed once the upstream Debian package carries the fix.

The fourteen CVEs are unauthenticated KDC/kadmind DoS and auth-indicator tampering that require the peer to be a KDC. This waiver is removed once the upstream Debian package carries the fix.

libkrb5support0 is the small support library (error tables, plugin loader, threading helpers) shared by the krb5 stack and is only loaded when libkrb5 initialises, which never happens in this image (no KDC, keytab, ccache or realm; local git bundles only). The fourteen CVEs live in KDC/kadmind request handling and are not reachable from the support-only code path. This waiver is removed once the upstream Debian package carries the fix.

liblastlog2-2 backs the lastlog2 login database introduced in util-linux 2.41; no login session is ever recorded because the entrypoint execs the control plane directly as 65534 and nothing calls login(1). The util-linux CVEs need privileged mount or nsenter paths, and this library is not part of the nsenter or mount-helper code. This waiver is removed once the upstream Debian package carries the fix.

This waiver is removed once the upstream Debian package carries the fix.

CVE-2025-69720 is a stack overflow in infocmp's analyze_string (progs/infocmp.c); infocmp is packaged in ncurses-bin, not in libncursesw6, so the vulnerable function is not part of this shared library at all. The library is present only so host-side tooling can format terminals, and the worker runs non-interactively. This waiver is removed once the upstream Debian package carries the fix.

CVE-2026-9538 is in Archive::Tar's _read_tar, a pure-Perl module, not in the interpreter shared library; libperl5.40 is linked by perl-base for Debian maintainer tooling. The worker never extracts tar archives through Perl: case bundles are unpacked by Python's tarfile with explicit member and size bounds. This waiver is removed once the upstream Debian package carries the fix.

libsmartcols1 formats columnar output for lsblk, findmnt and lsipc; the worker never invokes those tools and its own output is JSON, not human-readable tables. The util-linux CVEs require a privileged mount or nsenter operation, and no smartcols consumer that performs one is executed here. This waiver is removed once the upstream Debian package carries the fix.

libsqlite3-0 backs Python's sqlite3 module, but the production journal is PostgreSQL and the control plane never opens a SQLite database. The three CVEs need an attacker-populated FTS5 table with negative rowids and a prefix MATCH query (CVE-2026-119373/119374) or an attacker-crafted session changeset applied via the sessions extension (CVE-2026-119379); the worker builds and applies none of these. This waiver is removed once the upstream Debian package carries the fix.

CVE-2026-16742 is a systemd-homed privilege escalation via missing home-record signature verification. The image runs no systemd as PID 1, contains no homed daemon and manages no homed users, so libsystemd0 is only linked by packages that use sd_notify-style helpers. This waiver is removed once the upstream Debian package carries the fix.

CVE-2025-69720 is a stack overflow in infocmp (ncurses-bin); libtinfo6 is the terminal capability lookup library and does not contain progs/infocmp.c, so the vulnerable function is absent from this package. It is present only so non-interactive host tooling can resolve TERM entries. This waiver is removed once the upstream Debian package carries the fix.

CVE-2026-16742 is a systemd-homed privilege escalation; libudev1 is pulled in for device enumeration helpers. The image runs no udev daemon, no systemd-homed service and no systemd as PID 1, and the worker reads no device records. This waiver is removed once the upstream Debian package carries the fix.

ncurses-base ships terminfo database entries only and contains no executable code; CVE-2025-69720 is in infocmp's analyze_string inside ncurses-bin, so this data-only package cannot reach the vulnerable function. It is present because TERM lookup needs the compiled entries. This waiver is removed once the upstream Debian package carries the fix.

ncurses-bin ships infocmp, tic and toe, so CVE-2025-69720 (a stack overflow in infocmp's analyze_string when parsing a crafted terminfo source) is present in this package. The worker never runs infocmp/tic and never compiles terminfo from untrusted input; TERM is the Docker default and no terminfo source is parsed at runtime. This waiver is removed once the upstream Debian package carries the fix.

perl is present as a Debian maintainer/build dependency and the worker never runs a Perl script. CVE-2026-9538 requires Archive::Tar to read a crafted tar header with an unbounded size field, and no runtime path in this image parses tar archives with Perl. This waiver is removed once the upstream Debian package carries the fix.

perl-base is the essential minimal interpreter used by dpkg maintainer scripts; no maintainer script runs at image runtime. CVE-2026-9538 lives in Archive::Tar, which is packaged in perl-modules-5.40 rather than in perl-base, so the vulnerable module is not loaded by this package. This waiver is removed once the upstream Debian package carries the fix.

perl-modules-5.40 does contain Archive/Tar.pm, the module affected by CVE-2026-9538, so this is the one Perl package with the vulnerable source. It is only reachable from a Perl program that extracts an attacker-supplied tar header, and the worker never runs Perl: case bundles are unpacked by Python's tarfile with explicit bounds. This waiver is removed once the upstream Debian package carries the fix.

util-linux ships nsenter, dmesg, lsblk/findmnt and the mount.* helpers. CVE-2026-78408 is reached only through `nsenter --join-cgroup`, CVE-2026-76642 through a privileged external mount helper's post-hook, and CVE-2026-78409/78410 through X-mount.subdir and restricted bind mounting; every trigger needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN and a privileged mount or namespace syscall the worker never issues (uid 65534, cap-drop ALL, no --privileged, no host PID/namespace). This waiver is removed once the upstream Debian package carries the fix.

CVE-2026-124709 is a memory leak in openssl's QUIC stream handling that a peer triggers by sending crafted QUIC streams. In this image the only consumer of libssl3t64 is Python's TLS client stack for outbound HTTPS; neither the control plane nor the worker terminates or opens QUIC connections, so the trigger path is unreachable here. No Debian 13 package carries a fix yet: the pinned base digest ships 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 and even the newest trixie/main build, 3.5.9-1~deb13u1, is still reported affected. This waiver is removed once Debian publishes a fixed openssl, and the base digest is refreshed at that point.

CVE-2026-124709 is a memory leak in openssl's QUIC stream handling. The openssl CLI is installed by the base image but nothing in this repository invokes it, and the image never speaks QUIC, so the CLI cannot be driven into the vulnerable code path. No Debian 13 package carries a fix yet (3.5.7-1~deb13u3 installed, newest trixie/main 3.5.9-1~deb13u1 still affected). This waiver is removed once Debian publishes a fixed openssl, and the base digest is refreshed at that point.

No Debian 13 package carries a fix yet (3.5.7-1~deb13u3 installed, newest trixie/main 3.5.9-1~deb13u1 still affected). This waiver is removed once Debian publishes a fixed openssl, and the base digest is refreshed at that point.
